captures.name: frowning-slow
captures.findings: Ochre body and small gold hourglass visible; close protagonist overlap partly hides the lower body. This isolated angle does not establish crowded-room readability.

captures.name: gaper-slow
captures.findings: Slow hourglass visible above the head, foreshortened by the camera; lower body partly overlaps the protagonist. Warm body tint has limited contrast against the canyon ground.

captures.name: gusher-slow
captures.findings: Headless silhouette, blood column and airborne shot remain distinct; Slow cue visible. Probe records independent projectile time_scale=0.5.

captures.name: pacer-slow
captures.findings: Headless silhouette and Slow cue visible; no airborne shot in this frame, consistent with its contact-only controller.

captures.name: horf-slow
captures.findings: Stationary head, ochre tint and hourglass visible. Warm terrain reduces tint contrast, so the raised glyph provides the clearer status cue.

captures.name: horf-recovered
captures.findings: Hourglass and Slow tint are removed; pale head and attack windup cue/aim line are visible. Probe reports slow_frames=0.

captures.name: gaper-slow-freeze
captures.findings: Pale blue body and frost glyph take visual priority over Slow; no stacked hourglass clutter. The capture probe retains both timers. A still image alone cannot prove frozen motion.

limitations: Isolated native fixtures only; broader mixed-room, occlusion and camera-angle acceptance remains open.
Slow ochre is close to warm canyon ground and its small hourglass can be foreshortened. Freeze has stronger contrast.
Timing and projectile claims are supported by automated tests and probes, not by still screenshots.
Capture FPS is not a controlled performance benchmark.
